ops.title: cc-patch drops linux; daemonkit v0.21 is darwin-only and cc-patch could never patch on linux anyway
ops.body:
Decided by yasyf, 2026-08-02, during P4.5 W1.

daemonkit v0.21 does not compile off darwin by construction — no !darwin stubs, no runtime
unsupported-platform sentinels. cc-patch imports daemonkit/launchd, so GOOS=linux fails at the
build constraint.

Blast radius is wider than the migration lane first reported: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs test,
vet, AND lint (golangci-lint) and vuln (govulncheck) on ubuntu-latest. All four load the module for
GOOS=linux and fail identically (proved: GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go vet ./... fails on the launchd
constraint). .goreleaser.yaml declares goos: [darwin, linux], so a tagged release fails too.

CHOSEN: drop linux. goreleaser goos: [darwin]; the CI matrix and the lint and vuln jobs move to
macos.

Rationale beyond the constraint: cc-patch parses Mach-O only (internal/macho), shells out to
codesign, and installs LaunchAgents. The linux binary it publishes today cannot patch anything, so
the artifact was already nominal. Cost: published linux release assets disappear.

Rejected: //go:build darwin gating. It needs a !darwin sibling for internal/daemon AND for
internal/cli/daemons.go, or the two subcommands vanish from the linux binary — exactly the stub and
compat layer cc-patch STYLEGUIDE §1 and AGENTS.md § General Rules forbid. Also rejected: dropping
only the ubuntu CI leg, which leaves goreleaser declaring an artifact that cannot build.

SEPARATE AND STILL OPEN — the program path. service.StableProgram put the plist Program at
~/.daemonkit/bin/cc-patch, a byte copy that survived a package upgrade deleting the versioned
original. daemonkit.Stable() is reachable only through Daemon + Client.Ensure, and Program has no
exported path accessor, so cc-patch now resolves os.Executable() itself and the plist points at the
live Caskroom path. .goreleaser.yaml cask hooks.post.install re-runs install-daemons on install and
upgrade, but it is must_succeed: false — so a failed hook now leaves two agents pointing at a
deleted binary where before they kept working. Options: flip that hook to must_succeed: true; port
a stable-copy into cc-patch over durable.WriteFile; or export a path accessor on daemonkit.Program,
which would make this a one-line consumer change and serve every repo with a non-daemon
LaunchAgent.
